items.title: Equidimensionality and catenarity descend along a flat local map of Noetherian rings
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The statement says that for a flat local homomorphism A -> B of local Noetherian rings with B catenary and equidimensional, the fibres B over pB stay equidimensional and the source A is again catenary and equidimensional (statement lines 32388-32397). The proof reduces everything to one dimension computation: for a prime q minimal over pB the special fibre of A_p -> B_q is zero dimensional, so dim(A_p) equals dim(B_q), and equidimensionality plus catenarity of B make dim(B/q) independent of q (proof lines 32400-32413). The same computation applied to the quotients by a prime gives the dimension formula for A, and applied to an immediate specialization it shows that the dimension function drops by exactly one, which is the catenarity criterion (proof lines 32413-32434). The references to the dimension formula and to going down are pointers to standard results of another chapter; the argument that turns them into the two conclusions is inside the counted span.
